# Project Coordinator I

ATI Restoration, LLC

[Spring Valley, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Spring-Valley%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/-4695421073217040296?p=1&pos=0&rgn=7423&pageType=7&jobAge=20&jdpSource=101&jdpid=5707113782745992104&crId=US_0US_0)

Job Summary Project Coordinator provides complex administrative support to various members of the project team under the direction of the Office Manager. The Project Coordinator I will be responsible for project oversight and coordination of all its stages from inception to completion by inputting data, tracking, and monitoring control points and program updates. Additional responsibilities include assisting with document management and tracking progress for program estimates.
Job Summary Project Coordinator provides complex administrative support to various members of the project team under the direction of the Office Manager. The Project Coordinator I will be responsible for project oversight and coordination of all its stages from inception to completion by inputting data, tracking, and monitoring control points and program updates. Additional responsibilities include assisting with document management and tracking progress for program estimates.
Key Responsibilities Project & Workflow Management Intake new leads and jobs, entering all information across platforms to maintain a single, accurate source of data.
Under the guidance of the Office manager make decisions regarding project assignment to Project Directors to ensure proper project workflow.
Schedule initial inspections during the initial phone call to ensure parameters are met and provide a single point of contact.
Update platforms (XactAnalysis, Symbility, AlacNet) to meet program timelines for customer contact and site inspections.
Upload work authorizations and insurance-specific documents promptly to facilitate the release of funds.
Assist with securing third-party mortgage authorizations, coordinate mortgage inspections, and manage check endorsements.
Monitor JobTrack to ensure assignments are compliant and input job-specific milestones.
Review daily reports and the TPA/Contractor Connection Dashboard to maintain compliance, resolve discrepancies, and notify billing of any disputes.
Monitor job progress for USAA checks to ensure timely endorsement at final walk-throughs and verify check amounts against estimates.
Review completed project files for invoicing, ensuring all estimates, change orders, and close-out documents are accurate and accounted for.
Administrative Support Provide high-level administrative support to Project Directors and the Project Management team.
Conduct quality checks of purchase orders and administer work authorizations/COSs as needed.
Prepare job files and organize paperwork accurately using Salesforce.
Transfer and upload photos into specific files to forward to corporate staff.
Assist with reconciliation and sending billing reports to accounting staff by monthly deadlines and handle billing exceptions.
Generate requests to ensure promptness on estimates.
Attend all appropriate company training and monthly Admin Program meetings.
Execute administrative support functions and perform special project assistance as needed.
Qualifications And Experience High School Diploma or equivalent.
Minimum of 1 year of experience in a coordinator or administrative role.
Construction industry experience preferred.
Experience working in Salesforce, including generating reports (preferred).

## TRAVEL & WORKING CONDITIONS

Travel is minimal for this position.
This position requires sitting for long periods of time and looking at monitors along with typing for extended periods of time.
This position may require occasional flexibility in schedule to address urgent or time-sensitive employee relations matters.
Work is performed in a professional office environment.

**DEFINITION**

Under immediate or general supervision, receives 911 system emergency and non-emergency calls; dispatches assignments according to established emergency and County procedures; performs a variety of technical tasks relative to the assigned functional area; and performs related duties as assigned.

**SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED**

Receives immediate (Public Safety Dispatcher I) or general (Public Safety Dispatcher II) supervision from assigned supervisory or management personnel. Exercises no direct supervision over staff.

**CLASS CHARACTERISTICS**

_Public Safety Dispatcher I:_ This is the trainee-level classification in the Dispatcher series. Trainees work in the communications center and receive on the job training, specific day-to-day direction and are closely supervised. Incumbents at this level are not expected to function with the same amount of knowledge or skills as positions allocated to the II and Senior levels of the series. Initially under immediate supervision, incumbents learn and perform routine duties in support of public safety communications. Duties include frequent interaction with the public via telephone in both emergency and non-emergency situations. The position requires incumbents to receive, relay and provide accurate information, forms and reports to others within established legal guidelines. Once a Public Safety Dispatcher I completes training, and as incumbent demonstrates skill to perform the work independently, general supervision and frequent review of work lessen. Positions at this level develop the skills to perform most of the duties required of positions at the II level, but are not expected to function at the same skill level and exercise less independent discretion and judgment in matters related to work procedures and methods. Work is supervised while in progress and fits an established structure or pattern. Exceptions or changes in procedures are explained in detail as they arise.

_Public Safety Dispatcher II:_ This is the journey level classification in the Public Safety Dispatcher Series. Positions at this level have completed training and are fully competent to perform the full range of assigned duties. Positions at this level receive only occasional instruction or assistance as new or unusual situations arise and are fully aware of the operating procedures and policies of the work unit. This class is distinguished from the Senior Public Safety Dispatcher in that the latter performs the complex work assigned to the series and is responsible for providing lead direction and training to lower-level staff in the series.

Positions in the Public Safety Dispatcher class series are flexibly staffed; positions at the II-level may be filled by advancement from the I-level; progression to the II-level is dependent on (i) management affirmation that the position is performing the full range of duties assigned to the classification; (ii) satisfactory work performance; (iii) the incumbent meeting the minimum qualifications for the classification including any licenses and certifications; and (iv) management approval for progression to the II-level.

# Nonprofit Program Operations Coordinator (INTERNSHIP, Part-Time)

Location:Nashville, TNCompany:Healing Innovations, Inc.

## Description:

PROGRAM OPERATIONS COORDINATOR (INTERNSHIP, ~10 HRS/WEEK)

Nashville NeuroGym — a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by Healing Innovations, Inc.

Nashville, TN (on-site, with some remote work)

ABOUT US

Nashville NeuroGym is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit on a mission to redefine recovery for people living with neurological disorders. We pair advanced rehabilitation robotics with experienced clinical professionals to deliver activity-based programming that is personalized, goal-driven, and built to last. We have served more than 80 adults and children across Middle Tennessee living with stroke, spinal cord injury, MS, TBI, Parkinson's, cerebral palsy, and other neurological conditions.

Our program is built around Rise&Walk, an FDA-registered robotic rehabilitation system supporting seated, standing, and walking training in a single device. Participants come to us shortly after inpatient rehab, alongside outpatient therapy, or years after injury as an ongoing wellness tool.

Note: we are a wellness gym, not a physical therapy clinic, and we operate under the guidance of specialized physical therapists.

THE ROLE

We are looking for a Program Operations Coordinator to become the day-to-day operational backbone of the program. This is a volunteer role of roughly 10 hours per week, and it is broad by design. You will be the first voice a prospective participant hears when they call, the person who gets a demo on the calendar, the one chasing down a grant deadline, and the one making sure an event actually comes together.

This is a strong fit for a student or recent graduate who wants real ownership rather than a role shadowing someone else doing the work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Participant intake and follow-up — return calls from prospective participants and families, answer questions, and keep clear records

• Scheduling — coordinate demos, initial evaluations, and sessions with our clinical staff

• Referral outreach — build relationships with PTs, OTs, physicians, inpatient rehab units, and support groups across Middle Tennessee

• Grant research and applications — find opportunities that fit our mission, track deadlines, and help draft and submit

• Fundraising support — donor outreach, giving campaigns, sponsorships, and gift acknowledgment

• Marketing and communications — social content, participant stories, email updates, and outreach materials

• Event planning — open houses, demo days, community events, and fundraisers

• General operations — records, simple reporting, trackers, and the range of tasks that come with a small nonprofit

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• Comfortable on the phone. Many inquiries come from patients and families in a difficult moment. Be warm, be clear, and call people back.

• Self-directed. You'll often be the only person on a given task.

• Organized. You can hold a schedule, a grant calendar, and a referral list without being reminded.

• A capable writer. Grant applications, donor notes, and social posts all come out of this role.

• Discreet with health information and personal circumstances.

• Motivated by helping people regain mobility and independence.

Current students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply — especially in physical therapy, occupational therapy, exercise science, kinesiology, public health, nonprofit management, health administration, communications, or business. No prior nonprofit experience required.

WHAT YOU GET

• Hands-on experience running the operations of a nonprofit, with real ownership

• Exposure to advanced rehabilitation robotics alongside licensed physical therapists

• Citable accomplishments: grants submitted, events run, referral partnerships built

• Mentorship from our clinical and leadership team, and a reference from people who will know your work well

• Academic credit where your program allows — we're glad to work with your school's internship or practicum requirements, including supervisor sign-offs, learning objectives, and hour logs

THE DETAILS

• Volunteer, unpaid, approximately 10 hours per week

• On-site at 240 Great Circle Rd., Suite 333, Nashville, TN 37228, with some remote work

• Flexible around class schedules; availability needed on our operating days (currently Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday)

• As the program grows and funding allows, we intend for this to become a paid role, and we'd look first to the person already doing the work

HOW TO APPLY

Send a resume and a short note about why this program interests you to admin@nashvilleneurogym.com, or call (615) 965-5020 ext. 4. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Want to see the program first? We're happy to schedule a demo — therapists, physicians, students, and family members are all welcome.
